Each one\\u0027s handoff follows, in\\ndispatch order \\u2014 the run that opened the work first, its follow-ups after it.\\n\\n[Run 1 of 4 \\u00B7 a590110a]\\n\\n- The branch has the finished courier backoff. It adds a per-project \\u0060CourierFailureStreak\\u0060 document and a \\u0060CourierBackoffWaits\\u0060 helper. \\u0060CourierGate\\u0060 now takes the streak instead of a bool. \\u0060CourierEngine\\u0060 writes the streak in the same session as the run\\u0027s completion, and \\u0060ProjectPurgeEngine\\u0060 deletes it. It also adds a streak-aware \\u0060CourierStatusLine\\u0060, a \\u0060CourierDoctor\\u0060, a new ceiling option, and updated docs and tests.\\n- A streak document with Count 0 is a deliberate state (a daemon-ended courier\\u0027s hold). Use \\u0060CourierFailureStreak.IsRunning\\u0060, not the document\\u0027s existence, to tell whether a project is failing. The restart pull-in marker must be set on a project\\u0027s first tick whether or not a streak exists.\\n- Nothing was left undone. This run only checked the branch (clean, merges cleanly into the moved \\u0060origin/main\\u0060). The earlier PR push failed on a transient GitHub HTTP/2 error and is for the platform to retry.\\n\\n[Run 2 of 4 \\u00B7 6eedaa7c]\\n\\n- **What now exists:**\\n  - \\u0060OrchestratorFeedReader.ReadUndrainedAfterAsync\\u0060, a read from any sequence that leaves the cursor alone.\\n  - Paging in \\u0060CourierDoctor\\u0060, capped at 10 pages, with a \\u0060FeedCheckIncomplete\\u0060 fact and its own dim line.\\n  - A registration reset applied inside the \\u0060EndedByDaemon\\u0060 branch of \\u0060CourierEngine.RecordOutcomeAsync\\u0060.\\n  - Regression tests for both fixes.\\n- **Gotcha:** a zero-count \\u0060CourierFailureStreak\\u0060 is the daemon-ended hold. \\u0060WasResetByRegistration\\u0060 requires \\u0060Count \\u003E 0\\u0060, so applying the reset when the hold is written is what keeps the next tick from deleting it.\\n- **Left undone:** the incomplete-check path (a feed longer than 10 pages, about 20,000 events) is only covered by the \\u0060Evaluate\\u0060 unit test, not by an integration seed that large. A failed courier ending still builds on the old streak when the window re-registered mid-flight, but the next tick resets it anyway, so I left it.\\n\\n[Run 3 of 4 \\u00B7 4548ffbf]\\n\\n- **What now exists:** A registration reset keeps a daemon-ended courier\\u0027s hold, whether the window registered before or after that ending was recorded. The reset compares against the launch time of the registration the failed courier addressed, stored as \\u0060CourierFailureStreak.LastAddressedLaunchAt\\u0060, instead of its dispatch time.\\n- **Gotcha:** \\u0022The last ending was a daemon ending\\u0022 is inferred as the last run\\u0027s \\u0060CompletedAt \\u003E streak.LastFailureAt\\u0060. That works because every failure stamps \\u0060LastFailureAt\\u0060 with its own completion time and a delivery deletes the document. Keep that invariant if those writes ever change.\\n- **Left undone:** I didn\\u0027t rebase the branch onto the moved \\u0060origin/main\\u0060, because tree identity required keeping the old base and this was a review follow-up, not a rebase. I didn\\u0027t rerun the full suite (it\\u0027s the daemon\\u0027s gate).\\n\\n[Run 4 of 4 \\u00B7 558d73ac]\\n\\n- The local branch carries the three fixes from the 2026-11-06 window notes and is rebased onto \\u0060origin/main\\u0060 (\\u0060a6877f77c\\u0060). It is clean, merges cleanly, and is ready for the platform\\u0027s force-with-lease push. Comparing it with the pushed PR head also shows main\\u0027s newer commits (the Windows autostart changes) because of the rebase; those are not part of this PR\\u0027s own change.\\n- \\u0060CourierEngineTests.EngineFor\\u0060 takes any \\u0060IExecutor\\u0060, so a failing-spawn test only needs a small fake like \\u0060ThrowingExecutor\\u0060.\\n- I left the reset rule and both Copilot threads alone on purpose: they were declined and resolved earlier, and the identity-based reset is tracked as separate
